extracted.intended_audience: journalists, science communicators, researchers, and general public interested in AAAS news and press releases
extracted.subtask_description: A news index page listing recent AAAS statements, announcements, and science news with headlines, dates, short summaries, categories, and links to full items. Used to surface press releases and related communications for media and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline / Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The prominent title of each news item (e.g., 'AAAS Statement on Dismissal of National Science Board', 'Andrew Black named chief operating officer of AAAS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines are succinct descriptive labels for the content and appear as the primary link to the full item. Examples on page: 'AAAS Statement on Dismissal of National Science Board', 'Prize winner’s research reprograms tumor cells to trigger antitumor immunity'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Date
rubrics_metrics.description: The date associated with each item (e.g., 'April 26, 2026', 'April 20, 2026').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates are displayed with each entry and used to order recent items; they signal timeliness and are shown both inline with items and in the date-stamped listing (e.g., '26 Apr').

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline / Source Office
rubrics_metrics.description: The office or authoring unit shown for items (e.g., 'Office of Communications').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listing includes a source/byline indicating which AAAS office issued the piece; useful for attribution and for press contacts. Shown repeatedly in the listing rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category / Section Label
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorization of the item into types such as 'Statements', 'AAAS News', 'Science News'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items are tagged with a section to indicate content type or audience (example labels on page: 'Statements', 'AAAS News', 'Science News'), helping readers find relevant kinds of communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short summary / Teaser
rubrics_metrics.description: A one- or two-sentence summary or lead that briefly describes the content (e.g., 'As COO, Black will be responsible for stewarding the day-to-day operations of the organization...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teasers provide context and entice clicks; examples include summaries for appointments, fellowships, and prize announcements ('Fifteen early career scientists — spanning research areas from medical artificial intelligence to exoplanets to bug science — will join newsrooms...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-to-action / Link to full item
rubrics_metrics.description: An explicit link or prompt to read the full release (e.g., 'Learn More', 'Click to read the full statement.', 'More').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List view items include a CTA linking to the full article or statement. Verbatim cues on the page: 'Click to read the full statement.' and repeating 'Learn More' links; sidebar entries use 'More'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content topic / item type (announcement vs. statement vs. news)
rubrics_metrics.description: The substantive nature of the entry (examples on page include statements, personnel announcements, fellowship welcomes, letters to Congress, prize/winner stories, award announcements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site distinguishes item types by both category tags and content style — e.g., 'AAAS Statement' for organizational positions, 'AAAS News' for internal announcements, and 'Science News' for coverage pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing order and navigation (chronological and paginated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items are presented in a chronological list with a 'Load More' control for pagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page orders recent items by date and provides a 'Load More' button to retrieve older entries; sidebar also summarizes recent posts by date for quick navigation (e.g., repeated date snippets like '26 Apr', '20 Apr').
